subject: Intermittent truncated packets on private peering during Halcyon migration
messages:
From: NetOps Team <netops@halcyonhealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Jan 2028 15:04:20 -0800
Subject: Intermittent truncated packets over private peering — Halcyon migration

Hannah / Redwood team,

We started a migration of our application traffic to the new private peering circuit last night and are seeing a small but customer-impacting percentage (1–3%) of requests fail with truncated TLS handshakes or early TCP RSTs. The failures correlate with connections that traverse your EquiNet edge -> Redwood private link.

What we've captured so far:
- Packet captures show the server's TLS ServerHello fragmented — the responder's segment is ~1200 bytes and the client-side stack discards it; subsequent retransmit is fine.
- Path MTU on some flows appears to be negotiated lower than expected (observed 1380 MSS in SYN/ACKs from our router), but we still see 1500-sized fragments on the wire from one hop in the middle.
- Failures started immediately after we flipped to the new edge IP block (migration tag halcyon-mig-010).

Attached: halcyon_sample_trunc.pcap, halcyon_flow_logs.txt.

Can your side triage whether the Redwood edge is dropping or rewriting fragments, or whether an SG/NAT change is causing fragmentation asymmetry? This is affecting user logins; tagging as high priority.

Thanks,
Samir Patel
NetOps — Halcyon Health
netops@halcyonhealth.com

--
Attachment: halcyon_sample_trunc.pcap (pcap)
Attachment: halcyon_flow_logs.txt (txt)

Subject: Re: Intermittent truncated packets over private peering — Halcyon migration

Thanks Samir — looping in network on-call. Markus / Vanessa, Halcyon reports truncated TLS ServerHello fragments and asymmetric MTU behavior immediately after their migration. They attached a pcap and flow logs (see attachments).

Immediate asks:
- Markus: can you confirm whether any recent edge changes (iptables, conntrack, fragmentation handling, or MSS clamping) were deployed in the last 24 hours?
- Vanessa: please check routing policies / per-customer SNAT rules for Halcyon (tag halcyon-mig-010) and any security group rules that might drop fragments or reassemble incorrectly.
- Samir: can you confirm a few impacted timestamps (UTC) and the connection five-tuple for one failing request so we can correlate?

Severity: P1 for now; we can apply a temporary mitigation if we can identify candidate changes quickly.

Hannah

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Jan 2028 16:03:40 -0800
Subject: Re: Intermittent truncated packets over private peering — Halcyon migration

Triage update (quick notes from edge):
- I pulled the provided pcap and correlated it with our edge traces (edge-id eqn-usw-12). The responder packets that Halcyon flags are leaving our edge as two fragments (~1200B then the remainder) when the upstream hop enforces a lower MTU. The original origin MSS negotiation between client and our server was 1460 in SYN, so we are performing fragmentation on the edge.
- I also checked our recent deploys: no iptables changes in the last 36 hours. However, the dedicated SNAT appliance in front of eqn-usw-12 was restarted during the rekey window for the migration; its kernel had 'tcp_mtu_probing' disabled and no MSS-clamp was configured on the IPsec tunnel. That explains why our outgoing segments are larger and get fragmented mid-path.
- We are also seeing asymmetric return paths for ~2% of flows: return traffic takes a different upstream peer that has an 1400 MTU limit (likely a middlebox on the ISPs). That combination creates the truncation observed.

Proposed mitigations:
1) Short-term (apply now): enable MSS clamping on Redwood edge egress for Halcyon's route (clamp to 1360) and add conntrack entry refresh so mappings survive for the in-flight sessions — this reduces fragmentation risk. Impact: negligible for most traffic, should remove truncation
2) Mid-term: request Halcyon to enable MSS clamp on their VPN/CSR and permit IP fragments in their firewall SG for the peering subnets (allow fragmented packets through).
3) Long-term: add a regression test in our rollout for edge reboots that checks MSS and tunnel options before cutover.

I can push (1) in the next 10 minutes if you approve. I will also add a diagnostic snapshot (redwood_edge_diag.txt) to the thread.

-Markus
Senior Network Ops — Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.ai

Attachment: redwood_edge_diag.txt (txt)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: netops@halcyonhealth.com, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Jan 2028 16:22:10 -0800
Subject: Re: Intermittent truncated packets over private peering — Halcyon migration

Samir / Halcyon team,

Thanks for the quick report. Markus confirmed a likely MSS/tunnel-clamp gap combined with an asymmetric return path that enforces a lower MTU on ~2% of flows.

Action plan:
- Redwood will enable an emergency MSS clamp (1360) on the egress route for halcyon-mig-010 now; this is a safe, reversible change that should eliminate mid-path fragmentation.
- Halcyon: please enable an MSS clamp on your VPN/CSR and relax the fragment handling rule in your firewall (allow fragments for the peer subnets) so that fragments aren't dropped by your SG.
- We'll coordinate a 30-minute maintenance window tonight at 01:30 UTC to monitor effect and rollback if anything unexpected occurs.

Playbook: https://redwood.example.com/playbooks/private-peering-mss-clamp (runbook outlines commands and rollback steps).

Please confirm readiness for the 01:30 UTC window. We'll also attach final diagnostics after the change.

-Vanessa
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai

Date: Fri, 12 Jan 2028 10:12:03 -0800
Subject: Re: Intermittent truncated packets over private peering — Halcyon migration

Vanessa / Redwood team,

We enabled MSS clamping on our CSR and relaxed the fragment rule in our firewall. We observed the following during the 01:30 UTC window:
- Transaction failure rate dropped from ~1–3% to <0.1% within two minutes of clamping.
- Final pcap shows ServerHello delivered as a single segment where previously it was fragmented (attached: halcyon_sample_trunc_fixed.pcap).
- We did not see any negative impact on throughput or CPU on our VPN devices.

Thanks for the rapid response and for applying the egress clamp. Please leave the clamp in place while we schedule a follow-up to permanently reconcile tunnel MSS settings and add the suggested rollout test.

Samir Patel
NetOps — Halcyon Health
netops@halcyonhealth.com
